summary: Builder reproduces the rows byte for byte (44 rows, 0 lint failures) and 5 stored cases replay to the stored numbers, but the guard has a hole: a groove ring whose outer wall stops 0.1 mm short of a post's round outer wall is built and reported, with the wrong volume (4.5e-3 against OCCT, 1e-3 and 1.8e-3 in the other cases) and wrong faces (5 against 7). Neither the lip guard (ring ends only) nor the box-only wall check covers a cylinder radial wall, and no row discloses it.

replays.live: BUILT, FAIL dV 4.5e-3 dCOM 9.2e-4 faces OCCT 7 / truck 5
BUILT, FAIL dV 1.8e-3 dCOM 3.6e-4 faces 7 vs 5

replays.live: identical (OCCT wraps the angle, as the row says)

defects.feature: rows 20/21 (groove on a plain post) and the guard G10 (grazing)
defects.problem: A ring whose outer round wall ends 0.05 to 0.1 mm short of the post's own round wall leaves a thin cylindrical lip. It is built and reported with dVol 4.5e-3 / 1.0e-3 / 1.8e-3 against OCCT (bar 3e-4) and the wrong face count; grazing() checks ring ENDS for cylinders and a tangent round wall only for boxes. Silent wrong solid, not disclosed.
The row itself says a near-tangent round wall against a flat face of a non-box part is not refused by any guard, backed by only 3 probes; same family of hole as the blocking one.
The curved-volume bar 1.5e-4 x amplification was fitted after seeing the spin-fuzz data (disclosed by the row); the wider bar is only justified by an exact Pappus oracle.
